currentWorkspaceSourceSample.selection: 2400 evenly spaced point IDs from the filtered ledger; then 30 unique PostgreSQL chunk-ID matches with exact Qdrant/PostgreSQL chunk-hash equality and 30 with differing hashes
currentWorkspaceSourceSample.interpretation: Several differing Qdrant/PostgreSQL chunk hashes coexist with current-source file-hash and exact-substring matches, consistent with different chunk-hash recipes or stale payload fields; the bounded sample does not identify which or prove the indexed historical revision.

interpretation: No-unique-point-ID ownership is not equivalent to no PostgreSQL association: most reviewed points resolve to one atlas_packets row by payload packet_key.
The packet-key association is one-to-many: 103019 points map to 4546 packet keys, and most point IDs differ from the single atlas_packets.qdrant_point_id value.
Payload chunk_id and source_ref matches are partial; content hashes disagree for most unique chunk_id matches and their hash scopes are not proven equivalent.
These observations do not establish that points are duplicates, stale, unused, or safe to delete. No deletion, backfill, or projection is authorized by this audit.
